title: Effects of Different Training Intensity Distribution in Recreational Runners
publisher: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
claims: Thirty-eight recreational runners were randomized to a polarized endurance training group or a focused endurance training group for eight weeks, with programs balanced for total training impulse.
Target intensity distributions were 77/3/20 for the polarized group and 40/50/10 for the focused group.
Actual execution in the polarized group was 78% plus or minus 9.2% in zone 1, 3.1% plus or minus 1.3% in zone 2 and 18.9% plus or minus 4.6% in zone 3.
Both groups improved structural, functional and performance outcomes, with no significant between-group difference.
The polarized group accumulated 29.9 plus or minus 3.1 hours of training, while the focused group accumulated 24.8 plus or minus 2.0 hours, about 17% less time for similar improvements.
The paper cites a 10-week study in which polarized training improved 10 km performance by 5% versus 3.5%, but concluded that overall evidence was insufficient to support one model over another.
